graph.title: Make it Rain clap machine (Arduino MKR Zero)

new_part_types.name: ICS43432 I2S digital MEMS microphone breakout

notes: [E8] kept, not a real problem for this manual: the tutorial powers the DC motor from the MKR Zero's 5 V rail (low-side MOSFET switch, flyback diode, 0.1uF across the motor, 100uF on the supply), with an external battery only as an optional extra. The motor in the photo is the larger can motor from the Arduino starter-kit pack (product C000044), not the 1-3 V hobby motor that the catalogue 'dc-motor' entry describes, so the catalogue's 3 V rating does not match this project's motor. The catalogue has no closer 5 V-class motor, so dc-motor is kept and run on 5 V as the manual does.

Two 2.2k resistors are intentional: the Hardware text describes a pull-down on the motor MOSFET gate and a separate pull-up on the servo-signal MOSFET drain, and the component photo shows two resistors.
The rubber band is mechanical only (woven into the wheel) and is not in the graph.

The schematic image was not available, so wiring is derived from the hardware text: I2S mic SD=A6, SCK=pin 2, FS(WS)=pin 3; MOSFET + diode + pull-down switch the motor; MOSFET + pull-up level-shift the 3.3 V PWM to a 5 V servo signal.
MKR pins D4 (motor gate) and D5 (servo signal) are assumed. Breadboard rails: tp = 5V, tn = GND; mic LR tied to GND; mic 3V3 and q2 gate on MKR VCC (3.3 V).

Wire count/colours are estimated from the photos (17 male jumper wires). Catalogue substitutions: capacitor-22pf type used for the 0.1uF ceramic and capacitor-10uf for the 100uF electrolytic, values in props; diode and ICS43432 mic are new types.

graph_initial.title: Make it Rain clap machine (Arduino MKR Zero)

new_part_types.name: ICS43432 I2S digital MEMS microphone breakout

notes: The schematic image was not available, so the wiring is derived from the hardware text: I2S mic on SD=A6, SCK=pin 2, FS(WS)=pin 3; MOSFET + diode + 2.2k pull-down switches the DC motor; MOSFET + 2.2k pull-up to 5V level-shifts the 3.3V PWM to a 5V servo signal; 0.1uF across the motor and 100uF across the 5V/GND rails for noise.

Motor MOSFET q1: gate to MKR pin D4 with r1 (2.2k) pull-down to GND, source to GND, drain to motor terminal 2; motor terminal 1 to 5V; flyback diode d1 anode on drain, cathode on 5V; c1 (0.1uF) across the motor terminals.

Servo level shifter q2: gate to 3.3V (MKR VCC), source to MKR pin D5, drain to servo PWM and to 5V through r2 (2.2k pull-up). The MKR pins D4 (motor) and D5 (servo) are my assumption since the sketch/schematic was not visible.
Breadboard rails: tp = 5V, tn = GND. 5V comes from the MKR Zero 5V pin (USB powered). Mic LR is tied to GND; mic 3V3 on MKR VCC.

Step 1 corrections: the four male-to-female wires were changed to plain jumper-wire (servo/motor connect via male pins), and two jumper wires (wire16, wire17) were added, giving 17 wires total; exact wire count and colours are an estimate from the photos.
Rubber band and the laser-cut box are mechanical; the rubber band has no connections in the graph.
Catalogue substitutions kept from step 1: capacitor-22pf type used for the 0.1uF ceramic cap and capacitor-10uf type for the 100uF electrolytic (values in props).

final_issue_list: the graph has 2 x resistor, but the tutorial's parts list and circuit text describe at most 1: check each one against the tutorial and remove any it does not have
